---
- name: Install nftables
  community.general.pacman:
    name: nftables
    state: present

- name: Verify the configured physical DMZ interface exists
  ansible.builtin.assert:
    that:
      - "ai_dev_physical_interface in ansible_facts.interfaces"
    fail_msg: "Configured DMZ interface {{ ai_dev_physical_interface }} is not present."

- name: Remove the legacy physical-interface IPv6 entry from sysctl.conf
  ansible.builtin.lineinfile:
    path: /etc/sysctl.conf
    regexp: >-
      ^\s*net\.ipv6\.conf\.{{ ai_dev_physical_interface | regex_escape }}\.disable_ipv6\s*=
    state: absent

# networkd can re-enable IPv6 after systemd-sysctl has run. Keep the
# cloud-init network definition intact and override only physical IPv6 policy.
- name: Check the physical interface cloud-init network definition
  ansible.builtin.stat:
    path: "/etc/systemd/network/10-cloud-init-{{ ai_dev_physical_interface }}.network"
  register: ai_dev_network_definition

- name: Require the supported networkd configuration before adding its override
  ansible.builtin.assert:
    that:
      - ai_dev_network_definition.stat.exists
      - ai_dev_network_definition.stat.isreg | default(false)
    fail_msg: >-
      Expected the cloud-init networkd definition for {{ ai_dev_physical_interface }}.
      Inspect the active network manager before changing physical IPv6 policy.

- name: Ensure the physical interface networkd override directory exists
  ansible.builtin.file:
    path: "/etc/systemd/network/10-cloud-init-{{ ai_dev_physical_interface }}.network.d"
    state: directory
    owner: root
    group: root
    mode: "0755"

- name: Keep physical networking IPv4-only across reboots
  ansible.builtin.copy:
    dest: "/etc/systemd/network/10-cloud-init-{{ ai_dev_physical_interface }}.network.d/90-ai-dev-ipv4-only.conf"
    content: |
      [Network]
      DHCP=ipv4
      LinkLocalAddressing=no
      IPv6AcceptRA=no
    owner: root
    group: root
    mode: "0644"

- name: Persist IPv6 disable on the physical DMZ interface
  ansible.builtin.copy:
    dest: /etc/sysctl.d/90-ai-dev-dmz.conf
    content: |
      net.ipv6.conf.{{ ai_dev_physical_interface }}.disable_ipv6=1
    owner: root
    group: root
    mode: "0644"
  register: ai_dev_ipv6_config

- name: Read the physical DMZ interface IPv6 state
  ansible.builtin.command:
    cmd: "/usr/bin/sysctl -n net.ipv6.conf.{{ ai_dev_physical_interface }}.disable_ipv6"
  register: ai_dev_ipv6_state
  changed_when: false
  check_mode: false

- name: Disable IPv6 on the physical DMZ interface
  ansible.builtin.command:
    cmd: "/usr/bin/sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.{{ ai_dev_physical_interface }}.disable_ipv6=1"
  when: ai_dev_ipv6_config.changed or ai_dev_ipv6_state.stdout != "1"
  changed_when: true

# Resolved at run time, not committed: this repository is public.
- name: Resolve the docker-host tailnet address
  ansible.builtin.command:
    cmd: "tailscale ip -4 {{ ai_dev_docker_proxy_host }}"
  register: ai_dev_docker_proxy_address
  changed_when: false
  check_mode: false

- name: Resolve the Proxmox tailnet address
  ansible.builtin.command:
    cmd: "tailscale ip -4 {{ ai_dev_proxmox_api_host }}"
  register: ai_dev_proxmox_api_address
  changed_when: false
  check_mode: false

- name: Verify both Hermes egress peers resolved
  ansible.builtin.assert:
    that:
      - ai_dev_docker_proxy_address.stdout_lines | length == 1
      - ai_dev_docker_proxy_address.stdout | trim is match('^100\.')
      - ai_dev_proxmox_api_address.stdout_lines | length == 1
      - ai_dev_proxmox_api_address.stdout | trim is match('^100\.')
    fail_msg: >-
      Each Hermes egress peer must resolve to exactly one Tailscale IPv4
      address before ai-dev opens egress to it.

- name: Validate the optional media-broker port is separate
  ansible.builtin.assert:
    that:
      - ai_dev_hermes_media_broker_port | string is match('^[0-9]+$')
      - ai_dev_hermes_media_broker_port | int >= 1
      - ai_dev_hermes_media_broker_port | int <= 65535
      - ai_dev_hermes_media_broker_port | int not in [443, 2375, 8006]
    fail_msg: >-
      The optional media-broker port must be numeric and distinct from HTTPS,
      Docker observer, and Proxmox API ports.

# The distro unit's ExecStart loads /etc/nftables.conf. Keep that root-owned
# file as the administrator's persistent configuration and add only a native
# include for the fragment owned by this role.
- name: Check whether the persistent nftables configuration exists
  ansible.builtin.stat:
    path: /etc/nftables.conf
  register: nftables_root_config

- name: Reject an unconverted nftables root configuration
  ansible.builtin.command:
    cmd: >-
      /usr/bin/grep -Eq
      '^[[:space:]]*(flush[[:space:]]+ruleset|table[[:space:]]+inet[[:space:]]+(ai_dev|filter)([[:space:]]|\{))'
      /etc/nftables.conf
  register: nftables_legacy_config
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false
  check_mode: false
  when: nftables_root_config.stat.exists

- name: Require manual conversion before touching an ambiguous root config
  ansible.builtin.assert:
    that:
      - not nftables_root_config.stat.exists or (nftables_legacy_config.rc | default(1)) != 0
    fail_msg: >-
      /etc/nftables.conf contains flush ruleset or an inet ai_dev/filter table.
      Back it up, remove the legacy role definition and any global flush, merge
      unrelated rules manually, and rerun with ai_dev_allow_legacy_nft_migration=true
      only if the active inet filter table is confirmed to be legacy ai-dev state.
      The role will not parse or overwrite an ambiguous persistent file.

- name: Check whether the root configuration already includes nftables.d
  ansible.builtin.command:
    cmd: >-
      /usr/bin/grep -Eq
      '^[[:space:]]*include[[:space:]]+"/etc/nftables\.d/(\*\.nft|ai-dev\.nft)"[[:space:]]*$'
      /etc/nftables.conf
  register: nftables_root_include
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false
  check_mode: false
  when: nftables_root_config.stat.exists

- name: Reject an unrecognised nftables.d include form
  ansible.builtin.command:
    cmd: >-
      /usr/bin/grep -Eq
      '^[[:space:]]*include[[:space:]]+.*\/etc\/nftables\.d\/'
      /etc/nftables.conf
  register: nftables_any_include
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false
  check_mode: false
  when: nftables_root_config.stat.exists

- name: Require manual integration for an unrecognised nftables.d include
  ansible.builtin.assert:
    that:
      - not nftables_root_config.stat.exists
        or (nftables_root_include.rc | default(1)) == 0
        or (nftables_any_include.rc | default(1)) != 0
    fail_msg: >-
      /etc/nftables.conf has an nftables.d include in an unsupported form.
      Add the native /etc/nftables.d/ai-dev.nft or *.nft include manually,
      validate it with nft -c, and rerun the role.

- name: Record the root configuration integration state
  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    ai_dev_nftables_root_has_include: >-
      {{ nftables_root_config.stat.exists
         and (nftables_root_include.rc | default(1)) == 0 }}

- name: Ensure the native nftables fragment directory exists
  ansible.builtin.file:
    path: /etc/nftables.d
    state: directory
    owner: root
    group: root
    mode: "0755"

# Render and validate away from both persistent paths. A failed validation must
# not replace the last known-good fragment or root configuration.
- name: Render candidate nftables fragment
  ansible.builtin.template:
    src: nftables.conf.j2
    dest: /run/ai-dev-nftables.nft
    owner: root
    group: root
    mode: '0600'
  register: nft_candidate

- name: Read rendered media-broker firewall candidate
  ansible.builtin.slurp:
    src: /run/ai-dev-nftables.nft
  register: ai_dev_nftables_candidate_content
  check_mode: false
  when: not ansible_check_mode

- name: Verify rendered media-broker firewall state
  ansible.builtin.assert:
    that:
      - >-
        (ai_dev_hermes_media_broker_enabled | bool)
        == (('tcp dport ' ~ (ai_dev_hermes_media_broker_port | string) ~ ' accept')
            in (ai_dev_nftables_candidate_content.content | b64decode))
    fail_msg: >-
      The rendered nftables candidate must include the media-broker allow only
      when the opt-in integration is enabled.
  when: not ansible_check_mode

- name: Stage the root nftables configuration with the candidate include
  ansible.builtin.shell: |
    set -euo pipefail
    if [ -f /etc/nftables.conf ]; then
      cp -- /etc/nftables.conf /run/ai-dev-nftables-root.conf
    else
      printf '%s\n' '#!/usr/sbin/nft -f' > /run/ai-dev-nftables-root.conf
    fi
    if [ "{{ ai_dev_nftables_root_has_include | bool | ternary('1', '0') }}" -eq 0 ]; then
      printf '%s\n' 'include "/run/ai-dev-nftables.nft"' >> /run/ai-dev-nftables-root.conf
    fi
  args:
    executable: /bin/bash
  changed_when: false
  when: not ansible_check_mode

- name: Validate the candidate nftables fragment
  ansible.builtin.command:
    cmd: /usr/bin/nft -c -f /run/ai-dev-nftables.nft
  changed_when: false
  when: not ansible_check_mode

- name: Validate the staged persistent nftables configuration
  ansible.builtin.command:
    cmd: /usr/bin/nft -c -f /run/ai-dev-nftables-root.conf
  changed_when: false
  when: not ansible_check_mode

- name: Validate the candidate nftables transaction before installation
  ansible.builtin.shell: |
    set -euo pipefail
    apply_file=$(mktemp)
    trap 'rm -f -- "${apply_file}"' EXIT
    if /usr/bin/nft list table inet ai_dev >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      printf '%s\n' 'delete table inet ai_dev' >>"${apply_file}"
    fi
    if [ "{{ ai_dev_allow_legacy_nft_migration | bool | ternary('1', '0') }}" -eq 1 ] \
      && /usr/bin/nft list table inet filter >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      printf '%s\n' 'delete table inet filter' >>"${apply_file}"
    fi
    cat /run/ai-dev-nftables.nft >>"${apply_file}"
    /usr/bin/nft -c -f "${apply_file}"
  args:
    executable: /bin/bash
  changed_when: false
  when: not ansible_check_mode

- name: Install the validated nftables fragment
  ansible.builtin.copy:
    src: /run/ai-dev-nftables.nft
    dest: /etc/nftables.d/ai-dev.nft
    remote_src: true
    owner: root
    group: root
    mode: '0644'
  register: nft_ruleset
  when: not ansible_check_mode

- name: Create the root nftables configuration on a fresh host
  ansible.builtin.copy:
    content: |
      #!/usr/sbin/nft -f
      include "/etc/nftables.d/ai-dev.nft"
    dest: /etc/nftables.conf
    owner: root
    group: root
    mode: '0644'
  when:
    - not nftables_root_config.stat.exists
    - not ansible_check_mode
  register: nftables_root_file

- name: Add the owned fragment to an existing root configuration
  ansible.builtin.lineinfile:
    path: /etc/nftables.conf
    line: include "/etc/nftables.d/ai-dev.nft"
    insertafter: EOF
    owner: root
    group: root
    mode: '0644'
  when:
    - nftables_root_config.stat.exists
    - not ai_dev_nftables_root_has_include
    - not ansible_check_mode
  register: nftables_root_file

- name: Ensure nftables unit override directory exists
  ansible.builtin.file:
    path: /etc/systemd/system/nftables.service.d
    state: directory
    owner: root
    group: root
    mode: "0755"

- name: Install the nftables reload helper
  ansible.builtin.copy:
    src: reload-nftables
    dest: /usr/local/sbin/reload-ai-dev-nftables
    owner: root
    group: root
    mode: "0755"

- name: Prevent the distro nftables unit from flushing unrelated tables
  ansible.builtin.copy:
    dest: /etc/systemd/system/nftables.service.d/ai-dev.conf
    content: |
      [Service]
      RemainAfterExit=yes
      ExecStop=
      ExecStop=/bin/sh -c '/usr/bin/nft delete table inet ai_dev 2>/dev/null || true'
      ExecReload=
      ExecReload=/usr/local/sbin/reload-ai-dev-nftables
    owner: root
    group: root
    mode: "0644"
  register: nft_service_override

- name: Reload systemd after nftables unit ownership change
  ansible.builtin.systemd_service:
    daemon_reload: true
  changed_when: false

- name: Check whether the managed nftables table is loaded
  ansible.builtin.command:
    cmd: /usr/bin/nft list table inet ai_dev
  register: nft_table
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false
  check_mode: false

- name: Enable nftables at boot
  ansible.builtin.systemd_service:
    name: nftables
    enabled: true

# nft -c validates the complete transaction before nft applies it atomically.
# Existing managed tables are deleted inside that transaction; unrelated tables
# are never addressed. Deleting the legacy generic table is an explicit,
# operator-gated migration and is disabled by default.
- name: Validate and atomically load the owned nftables table
  ansible.builtin.shell: |
    set -euo pipefail
    apply_file=$(mktemp)
    trap 'rm -f -- "${apply_file}"' EXIT
    if /usr/bin/nft list table inet ai_dev >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      printf '%s\n' 'delete table inet ai_dev' >>"${apply_file}"
    fi
    if [ "{{ ai_dev_allow_legacy_nft_migration | bool | ternary('1', '0') }}" -eq 1 ] \
      && /usr/bin/nft list table inet filter >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      printf '%s\n' 'delete table inet filter' >>"${apply_file}"
    fi
    cat /run/ai-dev-nftables.nft >>"${apply_file}"
    /usr/bin/nft -c -f "${apply_file}"
    /usr/bin/nft -f "${apply_file}"
  args:
    executable: /bin/bash
  when:
    - not ansible_check_mode
    - nft_ruleset.changed or nft_table.rc != 0 or (ai_dev_allow_legacy_nft_migration | bool)
  changed_when: true

- name: Read the active nftables input chain
  ansible.builtin.command:
    cmd: /usr/bin/nft list chain inet ai_dev input
  register: ai_dev_nft_input_chain
  changed_when: false
  when: not ansible_check_mode

- name: Verify tailnet and DMZ input remain default-denied
  ansible.builtin.assert:
    that:
      - "'iifname \"tailscale0\" drop' in ai_dev_nft_input_chain.stdout"
      - "('iifname \"' ~ ai_dev_physical_interface ~ '\" drop') in ai_dev_nft_input_chain.stdout"
    fail_msg: Tailnet and physical DMZ input must remain default-denied.
  when: not ansible_check_mode

- name: Read the active nftables output chain
  ansible.builtin.command:
    cmd: /usr/bin/nft list chain inet ai_dev output
  register: ai_dev_nft_output_chain
  changed_when: false
  when: not ansible_check_mode

- name: Verify tailnet egress stays denied apart from the agent endpoints
  ansible.builtin.assert:
    that:
      - "'100.64.0.0/10' in ai_dev_nft_output_chain.stdout"
      - >-
        (ai_dev_docker_proxy_address.stdout | trim) ~ ' tcp dport '
        ~ ai_dev_docker_proxy_port ~ ' accept' in ai_dev_nft_output_chain.stdout
      - >-
        (ai_dev_proxmox_api_address.stdout | trim) ~ ' tcp dport '
        ~ ai_dev_proxmox_api_port ~ ' accept' in ai_dev_nft_output_chain.stdout
    fail_msg: >-
      ai-dev must reach the docker-host socket proxy and the Proxmox API while
      every other tailnet peer stays unreachable from this guest.
  when: not ansible_check_mode

---
- name: Ensure .config directory exists
  ansible.builtin.file:
    path: "/home/{{ username }}/.config"
    state: directory
    owner: "{{ username }}"
    group: "{{ username }}"
    mode: '0755'

- name: Ensure the Neovim site plugin directory exists
  ansible.builtin.file:
    path: "/home/{{ username }}/.local/share/nvim/site/plugin"
    state: directory
    owner: "{{ username }}"
    group: "{{ username }}"
    mode: "0755"

- name: Configure Neovim to copy through OSC 52
  ansible.builtin.copy:
    src: osc52.lua
    dest: "/home/{{ username }}/.local/share/nvim/site/plugin/osc52.lua"
    owner: "{{ username }}"
    group: "{{ username }}"
    mode: "0644"

---
# This integration is opt-in. Its helper owns only the marked media entry and
# token; disabled fresh/unowned hosts never probe Hermes runtimes or run the
# merge helper. Ownership metadata is read with the system Python as Hermes.
- name: Check whether the Hermes account exists
  ansible.builtin.getent:
    database: passwd
    key: "{{ ai_dev_hermes_user }}"
    fail_key: false

- name: Determine whether the Hermes account is available
  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    ai_dev_hermes_media_user_exists: "{{ ansible_facts.getent_passwd[ai_dev_hermes_user] is not none }}"

- name: Require the Hermes account outside check mode
  ansible.builtin.assert:
    that:
      - ai_dev_hermes_media_user_exists | bool or ansible_check_mode
    fail_msg: Provision the Hermes account before enabling its media integration.
  when: ai_dev_hermes_media_broker_enabled | bool

- name: Read bounded media ownership metadata as Hermes
  ansible.builtin.command:
    argv:
      - "{{ ai_dev_hermes_python }}"
      - -I
      - -c
      - |
        import json, os, stat, sys
        owned = False
        try:
            fd = os.open(sys.argv[1], os.O_RDONLY | os.O_NOFOLLOW | os.O_NONBLOCK)
            try:
                info = os.fstat(fd)
                if stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode) and info.st_uid == os.getuid() and info.st_size <= 256:
                    owned = os.read(fd, 257).startswith(b'ansible-managed-hermes-media-broker-v1\n')
            finally:
                os.close(fd)
        except OSError:
            pass
        print(json.dumps({'owned': owned}))
      - "{{ ai_dev_hermes_media_broker_marker }}"
  become: true
  become_user: "{{ ai_dev_hermes_user }}"
  environment:
    HOME: "{{ ai_dev_hermes_home }}"
  vars:
    ansible_python_interpreter: "{{ ai_dev_hermes_python }}"
  register: ai_dev_hermes_media_marker_probe
  changed_when: false
  check_mode: false
  timeout: 10
  no_log: true
  when: ai_dev_hermes_media_user_exists | bool

- name: Determine whether Hermes media files require reconciliation
  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    ai_dev_hermes_media_owned: >-
      {{ ((ai_dev_hermes_media_marker_probe.stdout | default('{"owned": false}') | from_json).owned) | bool }}
    ai_dev_hermes_media_runtime_needed: >-
      {{ (ai_dev_hermes_media_user_exists | bool)
         and ((ai_dev_hermes_media_broker_enabled | bool)
           or ((ai_dev_hermes_media_marker_probe.stdout | default('{"owned": false}') | from_json).owned | bool)) }}

- name: Validate the optional media-broker port
  ansible.builtin.assert:
    that:
      - ai_dev_hermes_media_broker_port | string is match('^[0-9]+$')
      - ai_dev_hermes_media_broker_port | int >= 1
      - ai_dev_hermes_media_broker_port | int <= 65535
      - ai_dev_hermes_media_broker_port | int not in [443, 2375, 8006]
    fail_msg: >-
      The media-broker port must be numeric and distinct from HTTPS, the Docker
      observer port, and the Proxmox API port.

- name: Require the operator media-broker token when enabled
  ansible.builtin.assert:
    that:
      - hermes_media_broker_token is defined
      - hermes_media_broker_token | string is match('^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{32,256}$')
    fail_msg: >-
      An operator-supplied media-broker token of 32-256 URL-safe characters is
      required when enabled.
  no_log: true
  when: ai_dev_hermes_media_broker_enabled | bool

# Resolved at run time, never committed: this repository is public. The same
# import-order dependency in firewall.yaml does not apply here because a
# hermes/hermes-media tagged run skips the firewall import entirely.
- name: Resolve the media-broker host tailnet address
  ansible.builtin.command:
    cmd: "tailscale ip -4 {{ ai_dev_docker_proxy_host }}"
  register: ai_dev_hermes_media_proxy_address
  changed_when: false
  check_mode: false
  when: ai_dev_hermes_media_broker_enabled | bool

- name: Require the fixed media-broker endpoint when enabled
  ansible.builtin.assert:
    that:
      - ai_dev_hermes_media_broker_host == ai_dev_docker_proxy_host
      - ai_dev_hermes_media_broker_url == ('http://' ~ ai_dev_docker_proxy_host ~ ':' ~ (ai_dev_hermes_media_broker_port | string) ~ '/mcp')
      - ai_dev_hermes_media_proxy_address.stdout_lines | length == 1
      - ai_dev_hermes_media_proxy_address.stdout | trim is match('^100\\.[0-9.]+$')
    fail_msg: >-
      The media broker must use the resolved docker-host Tailscale endpoint and
      its dedicated port.
  when: ai_dev_hermes_media_broker_enabled | bool

- name: Select a Hermes Python with YAML support
  ansible.builtin.command:
    argv:
      - "{{ ai_dev_hermes_python }}"
      - -I
      - -c
      - |
        import subprocess, sys
        try:
            result = subprocess.run([sys.argv[1], '-I', '-c', 'import yaml'],
                                    timeout=5, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
            sys.exit(result.returncode)
        except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
            sys.exit(1)
      - "{{ item }}"
  loop: "{{ ai_dev_hermes_config_python_candidates }}"
  become: true
  become_user: "{{ ai_dev_hermes_user }}"
  environment:
    HOME: "{{ ai_dev_hermes_home }}"
  vars:
    ansible_python_interpreter: "{{ ai_dev_hermes_python }}"
  register: ai_dev_hermes_media_python_probes
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false
  check_mode: false
  timeout: 10
  no_log: true
  when: ai_dev_hermes_media_runtime_needed | bool

- name: Set the verified Hermes media helper interpreter
  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    ai_dev_hermes_media_config_python: >-
      {{ (ai_dev_hermes_media_python_probes.results
          | selectattr('rc', 'defined')
          | selectattr('rc', 'equalto', 0)
          | map(attribute='item') | list | first) | default('') }}
  when: ai_dev_hermes_media_runtime_needed | bool

- name: Require a verified Hermes YAML interpreter
  ansible.builtin.assert:
    that:
      - ai_dev_hermes_media_config_python | length > 0
    fail_msg: >-
      No candidate Hermes Python interpreter with YAML support was found. Install
      YAML in the existing Hermes environment or set the approved candidate list;
      no package was installed automatically.
  when: ai_dev_hermes_media_runtime_needed | bool

- name: Install the Hermes media integration helper
  ansible.builtin.copy:
    src: manage-hermes-media.py
    dest: "{{ ai_dev_hermes_home }}/.local/bin/manage-hermes-media.py"
    owner: "{{ ai_dev_hermes_user }}"
    group: "{{ ai_dev_hermes_user }}"
    mode: "0700"
  become: true
  become_user: "{{ ai_dev_hermes_user }}"
  vars:
    ansible_python_interpreter: "{{ ai_dev_hermes_python }}"
  when: ai_dev_hermes_media_runtime_needed | bool

- name: Reconcile the optional Hermes media integration
  ansible.builtin.command:
    argv:
      - "{{ ai_dev_hermes_media_config_python }}"
      - "{{ ai_dev_hermes_home }}/.local/bin/manage-hermes-media.py"
      - --config
      - "{{ ai_dev_hermes_media_broker_config }}"
      - --env
      - "{{ ai_dev_hermes_media_broker_env }}"
      - --marker
      - "{{ ai_dev_hermes_media_broker_marker }}"
      - --url
      - "{{ ai_dev_hermes_media_broker_url }}"
      - --allowed-host
      - "{{ ai_dev_docker_proxy_host }}"
      - --allowed-port
      - "{{ ai_dev_hermes_media_broker_port }}"
      - --mode
      - "{{ 'enabled' if ai_dev_hermes_media_broker_enabled | bool else 'disabled' }}"
      - --takeover
      - "{{ 'true' if ai_dev_hermes_media_broker_takeover | bool else 'false' }}"
  become: true
  become_user: "{{ ai_dev_hermes_user }}"
  environment:
    HOME: "{{ ai_dev_hermes_home }}"
    MEDIA_BROKER_TOKEN: "{{ hermes_media_broker_token | default('') }}"
  vars:
    ansible_python_interpreter: "{{ ai_dev_hermes_python }}"
  register: ai_dev_hermes_media_reconcile
  changed_when: >-
    ai_dev_hermes_media_reconcile.rc == 0
    and (ai_dev_hermes_media_reconcile.stdout | from_json).changed | bool
  no_log: true
  timeout: 20
  notify: restart hermes user services
  when:
    - not ansible_check_mode
    - ai_dev_hermes_media_runtime_needed | bool

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -uo pipefail

readonly LOCAL_BIN="${HOME}/.local/bin"
readonly MOSHI_TARGETS='claude,codex,pi,gemini,antigravity,cursor,kimi,qwen,grok,omp'
export PATH="${LOCAL_BIN}:${HOME}/.nix-profile/bin:${PATH}"
USER=${USER:-$(id -un)}
export HOME USER

failures=()
declare -A tool_failed=()

tools=(claude codex pi herdr moshi)
declare -A tool_label=(
  [claude]='Claude Code'
  [codex]='Codex'
  [pi]='Pi'
  [herdr]='Herdr'
  [moshi]='Moshi'
)
declare -A tool_command=(
  [claude]='claude'
  [codex]='codex'
  [pi]='pi'
  [herdr]='herdr'
  [moshi]='moshi-hook'
)

usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: ai-dev-maintenance <ensure-present|update|status>

  ensure-present  Install missing tools, then reconcile integrations.
  update          Update every tool independently, then reconcile integrations.
  status          Report versions, integrations, and the Moshi runtime without changes.
EOF
}

run_step() {
  local label=$1
  shift
  printf '\n==> %s\n' "$label"
  if "$@"; then
    printf 'OK: %s\n' "$label"
    return 0
  fi

  printf 'FAILED: %s\n' "$label" >&2
  failures+=("$label")
  return 1
}

install_claude() {
  curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash -s stable
}

install_codex() {
  curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh | CODEX_NON_INTERACTIVE=1 sh
}

install_pi() {
  setsid --wait sh -c 'curl -fsSL https://pi.dev/install.sh | sh'
}

install_herdr() {
  curl -fsSL https://herdr.dev/install.sh | sh
}

install_moshi() {
  curl -fsSL https://getmoshi.app/install.sh | MOSHI_HOOK_SKIP_FIRST_RUN=1 sh
}

version_of() {
  local command_name=$1
  if command -v "$command_name" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    "$command_name" --version 2>&1 | head -n 1
  else
    printf 'not installed'
  fi
}

install_or_update_tools() {
  local mode=$1
  local tool command_name installer
  declare -A before=()

  for tool in "${tools[@]}"; do
    command_name=${tool_command[$tool]}
    installer="install_${tool}"
    before[$tool]=$(version_of "$command_name")

    if [[ $mode == ensure-present ]] && command -v "$command_name" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      printf 'PRESENT: %s: %s\n' "${tool_label[$tool]}" "${before[$tool]}"
      continue
    fi

    if ! run_step "${tool_label[$tool]} ${mode}" "$installer"; then
      tool_failed[$tool]=1
    elif ! command -v "$command_name" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      printf 'FAILED: %s installer did not provide %s\n' "${tool_label[$tool]}" "$command_name" >&2
      failures+=("${tool_label[$tool]} command verification")
      tool_failed[$tool]=1
    fi
  done

  printf '\nVersion summary:\n'
  for tool in "${tools[@]}"; do
    printf '  %s: %s -> %s\n' \
      "${tool_label[$tool]}" "${before[$tool]}" "$(version_of "${tool_command[$tool]}")"
  done
}

reconcile_integrations() {
  local mode=$1
  mkdir -p "${HOME}/.claude" "${HOME}/.codex"

  if [[ ${tool_failed[herdr]:-0} == 0 ]] && command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    local target
    # Vendor installers own generated integration files; Home Manager only owns
    # extensions maintained in this repository.
    for target in pi claude codex; do
      if [[ ${tool_failed[$target]:-0} == 1 ]]; then
        printf 'SKIPPED: Herdr integration: %s (tool update failed)\n' "$target"
        continue
      fi
      run_step "Herdr integration: ${target}" herdr integration install "$target" || true
    done
  fi

  if [[ ${tool_failed[moshi]:-0} == 0 ]] && command -v moshi-hook >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    if [[ ${tool_failed[claude]:-0} == 1 || ${tool_failed[codex]:-0} == 1 ]]; then
      printf 'SKIPPED: Moshi integrations (managed agent update failed)\n'
    else
      run_step 'Moshi integrations' moshi-hook install --target "$MOSHI_TARGETS" || true
    fi
    if [[ $mode == update ]]; then
      run_step 'Moshi user unit restart' systemctl --user restart moshi-hook.service || true
    elif ! systemctl --user is-active --quiet moshi-hook.service; then
      run_step 'Moshi user unit start' systemctl --user start moshi-hook.service || true
    fi
  fi
}

report_tool() {
  local label=$1 command_name=$2
  local version
  if ! version=$(version_of "$command_name"); then
    printf '%-12s %s\n' "${label}:" "version check failed"
    return 1
  fi
  printf '%-12s %s\n' "${label}:" "$version"
  [[ $version != 'not installed' ]]
}

status() {
  local failed=0
  printf 'ai-dev maintenance status\n\n'
  report_tool 'Node' node || failed=1
  report_tool 'Claude' claude || failed=1
  report_tool 'Codex' codex || failed=1
  report_tool 'Pi' pi || failed=1
  report_tool 'Herdr' herdr || failed=1
  report_tool 'Moshi' moshi-hook || failed=1

  printf '\nHerdr integrations:\n'
  if command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    herdr integration status || failed=1
  else
    printf 'not available\n'
    failed=1
  fi

  printf '\nMoshi runtime:\n'
  if command -v moshi-hook >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    moshi-hook status --json || failed=1
  else
    printf 'not available\n'
    failed=1
  fi
  systemctl --user is-active --quiet moshi-hook.service || failed=1
  if ! ss -H -ltn 'sport = :24543' | awk '{print $4}' | grep -Eq '^127\.0\.0\.1:24543$'; then
    printf 'Moshi listener is not contained on 127.0.0.1:24543\n' >&2
    failed=1
  fi

  return "$failed"
}

finish() {
  if ((${#failures[@]} > 0)); then
    printf '\nMaintenance completed with %d failure(s):\n' "${#failures[@]}" >&2
    printf '  - %s\n' "${failures[@]}" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  printf '\nMaintenance completed successfully.\n'
}

main() {
  local mode=${1:-}
  case "$mode" in
    ensure-present | update)
      install_or_update_tools "$mode"
      reconcile_integrations "$mode"
      finish
      ;;
    status)
      status
      ;;
    -h | --help | help)
      usage
      ;;
    *)
      usage >&2
      return 2
      ;;
  esac
}

main "$@"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -uo pipefail

# Runs Hermes-account maintenance from the management user, so no login to the
# agent account is needed. sudo acts as the hermes user and drives the hermes
# systemd user manager, which linger keeps running without a session.

readonly HERMES_USER=hermes
# Override point for tests; the deployment target is always /home/hermes.
readonly HERMES_HOME=${HERMES_MAINTENANCE_HOME:-/home/hermes}
readonly HERMES_BIN="${HERMES_HOME}/.local/bin"
readonly HERMES_PATH="${HERMES_BIN}:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin"

usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: hermes-maintenance <status|update|restart>

  status   Report tool versions and Hermes user-service state.
  update   Update the Hermes agent, Herdr, and Moshi for the hermes account,
           then restart its enabled user services.
  restart  Restart the enabled Hermes and Moshi user services.

Ansible (ai-dev role) owns the same operations in the steady state; this
command covers ad-hoc use between playbook runs.
EOF
}

run_as_hermes() {
  sudo -u "$HERMES_USER" env "HOME=$HERMES_HOME" "USER=$HERMES_USER" "PATH=$HERMES_PATH" "$@"
}

systemctl_user() {
  sudo systemctl "--machine=${HERMES_USER}@" --user --no-legend --no-pager "$@"
}

enabled_services() {
  systemctl_user list-unit-files --state=enabled 'hermes*.service' moshi-hook.service 2>/dev/null \
    | awk '{print $1}'
}

version_of() {
  local label=$1 binary=$2 out rc=0
  # Read through the sudo entry point: the hermes home is 0750, so a direct
  # executable test would always report not installed for other users.
  out=$(run_as_hermes "$binary" --version 2>/dev/null | head -n 1) || rc=$?
  if [[ $rc -eq 0 && -n $out ]]; then
    printf '%-10s %s\n' "${label}:" "$out"
  else
    printf '%-10s %s\n' "${label}:" 'not installed'
    return 1
  fi
}

status() {
  local failed=0
  printf 'Hermes account (%s) tools:\n' "$HERMES_USER"
  version_of Hermes "${HERMES_BIN}/hermes" || failed=1
  version_of Herdr "${HERMES_BIN}/herdr" || failed=1
  version_of Moshi "${HERMES_BIN}/moshi-hook" || failed=1

  printf '\nHermes user services (enabled):\n'
  local units unit
  units=$(enabled_services)
  if [[ -z $units ]]; then
    printf 'none\n'
    return "$failed"
  fi
  while IFS= read -r unit; do
    printf '%-28s %s\n' "$unit" "$(systemctl_user is-active "$unit" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  done <<<"$units"
  return "$failed"
}

restart() {
  local units unit
  units=$(enabled_services)
  if [[ -z $units ]]; then
    printf 'No enabled hermes*.service or moshi-hook.service units; nothing to restart.\n'
    return 0
  fi
  # Pick up drop-in changes (such as the moshi gateway listen override).
  systemctl_user daemon-reload || true
  local failed=0
  while IFS= read -r unit; do
    printf 'Restarting %s\n' "$unit"
    systemctl_user restart "$unit" || failed=1
  done <<<"$units"
  ((failed == 0))
}

update() {
  local failed=0
  printf '==> Hermes update\n'
  # hermes update exits 1 when its own gateway restart fails after a
  # successful update; the restart below replaces that mechanism.
  local out rc=0
  out=$(run_as_hermes "${HERMES_BIN}/hermes" update 2>&1) || rc=$?
  printf '%s\n' "$out"
  if ((rc != 0)) && ! grep -q 'Update complete!' <<<"$out"; then
    printf 'FAILED: Hermes update\n' >&2
    failed=1
  fi
  printf '==> Herdr update\n'
  run_as_hermes sh -c 'curl -fsSL https://herdr.dev/install.sh | sh' || failed=1
  printf '==> Moshi update\n'
  run_as_hermes sh -c 'curl -fsSL https://getmoshi.app/install.sh | MOSHI_HOOK_SKIP_FIRST_RUN=1 sh' || failed=1
  run_as_hermes "${HERMES_BIN}/moshi-hook" install --target hermes || failed=1
  printf '\n'
  status || failed=1
  printf '\n'
  restart || failed=1
  return "$failed"
}

case "${1:-}" in
  status | update | restart)
    "$1"
    ;;
  -h | --help | help)
    usage
    ;;
  *)
    usage >&2
    exit 2
    ;;
esac

# Hermes media-broker ownership and updates

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD013 -->

Portainer owns the read-only broker as an **ordinary Git-connected stack**
named `media-broker`, using the same repository source and polling as every
other inventoried stack. The application source and its container image live
in the dedicated [`mich-murphy/media-broker`](https://github.com/mich-murphy/media-broker)
repository; this repository owns only the stack definition at
`docker/media-broker/compose.yml` and the host policy around it.

This describes the target state. Until the one-time migration runbook below
is performed, the live stack is still the earlier manually updated one.

## Deployment pipeline

Merging to `main` in the media-broker repository deploys without manual host
steps, using the same digest-pin trigger every other stack relies on:

1. **Publish**: the media-broker repository's CI runs the source suite and,
   on merge to `main`, pushes the image to GHCR as
   `ghcr.io/mich-murphy/media-broker:main` plus an immutable `:sha-<commit>`
   tag kept for rollback and audit.
2. **Pin**: the Compose reference here is `:main@sha256:<digest>`. Renovate
   (already authenticating to ghcr.io as `mich-murphy` via its hostRules)
   updates the digest whenever `:main` moves and automerges the PR under the
   repository's existing digest-automerge rule. Renovate runs on a cron
   schedule; use its workflow dispatch to pin a fresh release immediately.
3. **Redeploy**: the digest bump is a commit on home-infra `main` — exactly
   the change Portainer's Git polling watches. It redeploys the stack and
   pulls the pinned digest.

The digest pin is the deploy trigger, not a style preference: Portainer's
auto-update compares repository commit hashes and never consults the
registry, so an unpinned moving tag would stay stale until an unrelated
commit happened to land. Portainer's only registry-aware feature is an
inbound registry webhook, which is unusable here (nothing gets through
Tailscale, and GHCR does not offer registry webhooks).

Rollback is `git revert` of the digest-bump commit (Portainer redeploys the
previous digest on the next poll) or an emergency editor update pinning a
known `:sha-<commit>` tag. Do not re-add a `build:` block to the Compose
file; Portainer must never build this image (see history below).

## Why this stack was previously manual

The broker used to be a host-built candidate: the image
`home-infra/media-broker:candidate` was built from a root-owned checkout on
docker-host, which forced manual updates and caused two documented incidents:

- Portainer 2.45 schedules polling **by Git source, not by stack**. Creating
  the broker on the repository's shared polling source redeployed it on source
  ticks despite a manual-only policy. See the
  [2.45 source scheduler](https://github.com/portainer/portainer/blob/2.45.0/api/gitops/scheduling/scheduler.go).
- Portainer 2.45 can rebuild a stack from its **retained Git context** when a
  `build` block is present, even with `PullImage: false`. During the MCP SDK
  patch rollout this replaced a freshly built image with stale source.

Publishing a registry image from dedicated repository CI removes the root
cause of both: there is no build block to exploit, no host checkout to
reconcile, and a redeploy can only pull an immutable digest. The broker is now
explicitly allowed on the shared Git source; the earlier "do not connect this
stack" rule is obsolete and must not be reintroduced while the image comes
from GHCR.

## Stack configuration

- Stack and Compose project: `media-broker`; container: `media-broker`
- Compose path: `docker/media-broker/compose.yml` (image-only)
- Image: `ghcr.io/mich-murphy/media-broker:main@sha256:...` (Renovate-pinned;
  unpinned only briefly before Renovate's first pin after introduction)
- Registry credentials: the package is private, so Portainer needs a `ghcr.io`
  registry entry. This is manual UI state, not established by this repository;
  add it in migration step 3 and audit it after a restore
- Update policy: shared Git polling; Renovate digest bumps are the trigger

Portainer supplies the interpolated `SONARR_URL`, `RADARR_URL`, `LIDARR_URL`,
`TAUTULLI_URL`, `MEDIA_BROKER_BIND`, `MEDIA_BROKER_BIND_HOST`,
`MEDIA_BROKER_ALLOW_PUBLIC_BIND`, and optional `MEDIA_BROKER_SECRETS_DIR`.
These values are URLs, nonsecret bind settings, and a host directory path.
Compose fixes the secret-file paths and the Host/Origin allow-lists. Never put
a backend API key or broker bearer value in Portainer's stack variables,
Compose environment, Git, or command arguments.

The fixed endpoint is `http://docker-host:8765/mcp`, with Host
`docker-host:8765` and Origin `http://docker-host:8765`. The host port binds
only the docker-host Tailscale IPv4. It is not exposed through Traefik, a LAN
exception, or shared port 443. The broker runs nonroot with a read-only
filesystem and has no Docker socket or media mounts.

## Host-side controls that remain

- The five files in `/etc/media-broker/secrets` (`broker-token`,
  `sonarr-api-key`, `radarr-api-key`, `lidarr-api-key`, `tautulli-api-key`)
  stay host-managed: directories `root:65532` mode `0750`, files
  `root:65532` mode `0640`. File-backed Compose secrets do not enforce their
  declared ownership or mode, so verify these after any host rebuild.
  Future ai-dev Ansible runs require the existing bearer as
  `hermes_media_broker_token` through protected variables.
- The host firewall admits TCP 8765 only from ai-dev's exact Tailscale
  address through `tailscale0`; the `docker-host` role defines and asserts
  the `DOCKER-USER` rules on every run.
- The broker uses a 5 MiB upstream-response bound for the observed 2.27 MiB
  Lidarr inventory.

## One-time migration runbook

Performed once, from the old manual stack to the Git stack. Steps 3 onward
assume the pull request introducing `docker/media-broker/compose.yml` has
already merged, because Portainer resolves that path from `refs/heads/main`.

1. Merge that pull request to `main` and confirm the Compose file resolves
   there.
2. Ensure the first image exists: the media-broker repository's `publish`
   job must have run on `main` so GHCR serves
   `ghcr.io/mich-murphy/media-broker:main`.
3. In Portainer, add `ghcr.io` registry credentials with pull access to the
   private package (classic PAT with `read:packages`). Skip this step if the
   package is made public.
4. Delete the existing `media-broker` stack (brief downtime; the old
   container name `media-broker-candidate` goes away with it). Do not delete
   host secret files.
5. Recreate the stack from Git: repository
   `https://github.com/mich-murphy/home-infra.git`, reference
   `refs/heads/main`, compose path `docker/media-broker/compose.yml`, the
   same nonsecret environment values as before, AutoUpdate polling enabled on
   the shared source. No relative-path volumes are needed for this stack.
6. Wait for the container to become healthy, then verify: the running image
   is the current `:main` build; authenticated reads from Hermes succeed for
   all four tools; unauthenticated requests are rejected; a different client
   is denied. Retain the existing ACL and token. No Hermes gateway restart
   is required.
7. Confirm Renovate opens and automerges the initial digest-pin PR for the
   image, and that Portainer redeploys on it. From then on, every
   media-broker merge becomes a Renovate digest bump → automerge → Portainer
   redeploy. If Renovate cannot resolve the digest, its token lacks
   `read:packages` for the private package — fix the token before relying on
   the pipeline.

This remains a read-only integration. Conversation-approved writes and
Jellyfin playback reporting are not enabled. Host controls are operational
policy, not a security boundary against root administrators.

I've been through the whole deployment. Here's the picture and what the change would mean.

## How ai-dev is deployed today

The same VM carries two distinct halves, which the `ai-dev` Ansible role provisions in sequence:

**Your remote dev environment** (the `michael` management user):
- **Terraform**: `proxmox_virtual_environment_vm.ai_dev` (VMID 110, Arch, 4 cores / 3 GiB / 150 GiB, vmbr1 DMZ), cloud-init snippet (`main.tf`, `cloud_init.tftpl` arch branch)
- `bootstrap.yaml` — pacman packages incl. Neovim + LSPs/formatters, paru/AUR (tflint, marksman), **Determinate Nix**, fish login shell, linger
- `home-manager.yaml` — clones your `nix-config`, asserts clean ff-only `main`, builds/activates `homeConfigurations."michael@ai-dev"`
- `accounts.yaml` — vaulted personal + BusinessCraft git identities
- `tools.yaml` — `ai-dev-maintenance` (installs/updates Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Herdr, Moshi for you), Node ≥22.19 assertion for Pi
- `neovim.yaml` — OSC52 site plugin
- `scratch.yaml` — disk-backed `TMPDIR` for your coding agents' scratch
- Your Moshi daemon on `127.0.0.1:24543`

**The Hermes agent** (the isolated `hermes` account):
- `hermes.yaml` — account, Hermes/Herdr/Moshi installs, scoped credentials, mosh timeout
- `hermes-media.yaml` — media-broker MCP integration
- `firewall.yaml`, `identity.yaml`, `system-maintenance.yaml`, handlers, `hermes-maintenance`

## What you'd remove

| Area | Files/changes |
|---|---|
| Home Manager | `tasks/home-manager.yaml` deleted; Determinate Nix install dropped from `bootstrap.yaml`; the whole nix-config build/activate machinery and its assertions |
| Your coding-agent toolchain | `tasks/tools.yaml` reduced to just installing `files/hermes-maintenance` (drop `ai-dev-maintenance` + Node assertion); `files/ai-dev-maintenance` and `ansible/tests/ai-dev-maintenance.sh` deleted |
| Git identities | `tasks/accounts.yaml` deleted; `host_vars/ai-dev.yaml` deleted; `ai_dev_git_user_emails` keys removed from the vault |
| Editor stack | `tasks/neovim.yaml` + `files/osc52.lua` deleted; `bootstrap.yaml` package list shrinks to a minimal set (drop neovim, stylua, gopls, delve, ruff, markdownlint-cli, nodejs, paru/AUR entirely) |
| Scratch space | `tasks/scratch.yaml` + `templates/tmpfiles-scratch.conf.j2` likely deleted — that existed for Claude/Bun/Pi scratch under `/var/tmp/michael` (or optionally retarget to `hermes`) |
| Docs | `docs/ai-dev.md` loses most of its bulk (mobile workflow for your user, interactive setup, git identity checks, Neovim exception, scratch section, verification of dev tools); `CONTEXT.md` loses the "ai-dev maintenance" entry; `README.md` architecture line and role-table row reworded |
| CI | `_quality-gate.yaml` shellcheck/test lists drop the deleted files |
| Role wiring | `main.yaml` drops the six imports, leaving identity → slim bootstrap → firewall → system-maintenance → hermes → hermes-media |

## What stays untouched

Terraform VM/cloud-init/DMZ placement, the common role (you still need the `michael` admin account for Ansible/SSH), `identity.yaml` (Tailscale SSH-off is load-bearing for Moshi on the hermes account too), all of nftables, earlyoom + timers, everything Hermes, the docker-host observer and media-broker, all hermes tests.

## Simplifications this unlocks

1. **The Moshi port collision goes away.** The hermes daemon sits on `127.0.0.1:24544` only because your daemon holds `:24543` (`ai_dev_hermes_moshi_gateway_listen` + the systemd drop-in in `hermes.yaml`). With no management-user Moshi, hermes reverts to the default port — delete the override and the variable, and the Moshi app's second-host entry simplifies.
2. **earlyoom** `--prefer` list is tuned for dev workloads (tsc, bun, esbuild, cargo...) and can shrink to just `node` (the Hermes gateway runtime).
3. The `/home/michael` 0750 assertion in `hermes.yaml` becomes mostly hygiene rather than load-bearing, since your home no longer holds gh tokens or agent sessions — I'd keep it anyway.

## Things to talk through

1. **VM spec**: 150 GiB disk and 4 cores were sized for dev work (node_modules, builds, Playwright). Hermes is described as "the largest install on the VM" already, so maybe fine — but worth deciding whether to rightsize. Disk can't shrink in place, so that means a rebuild if you want it smaller.
2. **Naming**: if the VM is purely the Hermes host, do you rename host/tag (`ai-dev` → `hermes`)? That touches the tailnet tag, grants, hosts.ini, docs — cheap to do now, annoying later. Or keep `ai-dev` as the DMZ-sandbox name regardless of persona.

# earlyoom sends SIGTERM to the largest process when both available memory and
# free swap fall below these percentages (SIGKILL at half of each). Preferred
# victims are the agent's transient runtimes (Playwright browser, the Node
# gateway); the Python agent, Herdr, and Moshi stay protected.

ai_dev_earlyoom_swap_percent: 8
ai_dev_earlyoom_avoid: "(^|/)(init|systemd.*|sshd.*|mosh-server|tailscaled|herdr|moshi-hook|dbus-broker.*)$"
ai_dev_earlyoom_prefer: "(^|/)(chrome|headless_shell|node)$"

summary:
## Goal
Repurpose the `ai-dev` VM in `/Users/mm/dev/home-infra` from a dual-purpose box (user's remote dev environment + Hermes infrastructure agent) into a host that runs only the Hermes agent under the isolated `hermes` account. Includes parallel cleanup of the `ai-dev` Home Manager configuration in `/Users/mm/dev/nix-config` (sibling repo, Mac-only after cleanup). Implementation has not started; planning is complete.

## Constraints & Preferences
- Keep the VM spec exactly as-is (VMID 110, 4 cores / 3 GiB / 150 GiB, vmbr1 DMZ) — no Terraform changes at all
- **Do NOT rename anything** (user reversed an earlier decision to rename `ai-dev` → `hermes`): keep hostname, role name `ai-dev`, `hosts.ini` group `[ai_dev]`, variable prefix `ai_dev_*`, tailnet tag `tag:ai-dev`, docs filenames, all cross-references
- Remote development is dropped entirely; ad-hoc dev on the host is acceptable via the hermes account if ever needed
- Interactive first-run setup reduces to `hermes setup` + Moshi pairing (already the documented flow)

## Progress
### Done
- [x] Full inventory of the ai-dev deployment across Terraform, Ansible, docs, CI, Docker, and nix-config
- [x] All design decisions made (VM spec, no rename, drop remote dev, nix-config cleanup in scope)
- [x] Final consolidated removal/simplification plan agreed (verbatim below)

### In Progress
- [ ] Awaiting user's go-ahead on "Shall I start on the home-infra PR?" — next action is implementing the home-infra changes

### Blocked
- (none)

## Key Decisions
- **No rename**: avoids the entire churn of Terraform `moved` blocks, tailnet tag/grant changes, on-host artifact renames, nftables table migration, and docs renames
- **Terraform untouched**: zero changes to `terraform/main.tf`, `cloud_init.tftpl`, variables
- **Management user `michael` stays** as a pure Ansible/SSH admin account (common role); only its dev tooling is removed
- **Moshi port simplification applies**: management user's daemon goes away, so hermes reverts to default `127.0.0.1:24543` and the `ai_dev_hermes_moshi_gateway_listen` override + systemd drop-in are deleted
- **On-host leftovers left inert**: michael's Nix store, `/home/michael/dev/nix-config`, and stale moshi unit not torn down by the role (optional manual cleanup)

## Next Steps
1. Get confirmation, then implement the home-infra PR:
   - Delete from `ansible/roles/ai-dev/`: `tasks/home-manager.yaml`, `tasks/accounts.yaml`, `tasks/neovim.yaml`, `tasks/scratch.yaml`, `files/ai-dev-maintenance`, `files/osc52.lua`, `templates/tmpfiles-scratch.conf.j2`; delete `ansible/tests/ai-dev-maintenance.sh`, `ansible/host_vars/ai-dev.yaml`
   - Reduce `tasks/tools.yaml` to only installing `files/hermes-maintenance` (remove `ai-dev-maintenance` install + Node ≥22.19 assertion)
   - Slim `tasks/bootstrap.yaml`: drop Determinate Nix install, paru/AUR, neovim + LSPs/formatters, nodejs, fish, michael's linger; keep pacman upgrade, packages `git openssh mosh curl jq python`, logind `KillUserProcesses=no`, locale
   - Remove Moshi gateway-listen override from `tasks/hermes.yaml` + delete `ai_dev_hermes_moshi_gateway_listen` from `defaults/main.yaml`
   - Retune earlyoom `--prefer` in `defaults/main.yaml` from `tsc|bun|node|next-build|esbuild|vitest|jest|cargo|rustc|go` to agent runtimes (`node`, headless chromium)
   - Remove imports from `tasks/main.yaml` keeping: identity → bootstrap → firewall → system-maintenance → tools (hermes-maintenance only) → hermes → hermes-media
   - Vault (`ansible/group_vars/secrets.yaml`): remove `ai_dev_git_user_emails`
   - Docs: gut dev-environment sections from `docs/ai-dev.md`; update `README.md` (architecture line, role table), `CONTEXT.md` (collapse "ai-dev provisioning"/"ai-dev maintenance" language entries), `docs/proxmox-host.md`; update `.github/workflows/_quality-gate.yaml` (remove deleted files from shellcheck/test lists)
   - Fold in the 1Password drift doc fix (see Critical Context)
2. Merge home-infra PR → run `ansible --limit ai-dev` (no terraform apply, no tailnet admin work, no docker-host run)
3. nix-config PR (can merge after): delete `hosts/ai-dev.nix` + `hosts/ai-dev-runtime.nix`; edit `flake.nix` (drop `aiDev`, `homeConfigurations."michael@ai-dev"`, `checks.x86_64-linux`, `x86_64-linux` from `systems`, update description); delete `ai-dev` host block in `home/ssh.nix`; delete `build-linux` job in `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`; update `README.md` (retitle, drop ai-dev deployment section), `AGENTS.md`, `TODO.md` (close the Neovim bootstrap item as moot). Keep all shared `home/*.nix` modules (used by Mac)
4. Phone: delete the old management-user Moshi host entry, keep the hermes one

## Critical Context
- **Role structure** (`ansible/roles/ai-dev/tasks/main.yaml` import order): identity → bootstrap → firewall → system-maintenance → scratch → home-manager → accounts → tools → neovim → hermes → hermes-media. Keep: identity, firewall, system-maintenance, hermes, hermes-media
- **Untouched surfaces**: `terraform/` entirely; `hosts.ini` (`[ai_dev] ai-dev ansible_user=michael`); `group_vars/ai_dev.yaml` filename; tailnet grants; docker-host role; Docker stacks (agent-observer, media-broker); hermes tests (`hermes-maintenance.sh`, `hermes-media*.sh`)
- **1Password drift found**: `docs/ai-dev.md` instructs creating two distinct fields (`tailscale docker-host authkey`, `tailscale ai-dev authkey`) but `terraform/main.tf` reads one shared `tailscale authkey` field for both (`local.scp["tailscale authkey"]`). Assistant proposed fixing the doc in the rewrite; user hasn't explicitly confirmed
- **Key vars** in `defaults/main.yaml`: `ai_dev_hermes_user: hermes`, `ai_dev_hermes_home: /home/hermes`, `ai_dev_hermes_moshi_gateway_listen: 127.0.0.1:24544` (to delete), `ai_dev_earlyoom_*`, `ai_dev_hermes_media_broker_*`
- **group_vars/ai_dev.yaml** keeps: `username: michael`, `ssh_public_key`, `ai_dev_hermes_authorized_keys`, hostname/interface/gateway/DMZ peers, media broker flag, swap settings; `user_shell: /usr/bin/fish` may be dropped
- **nix-config flake.nix**: `aiDev = home-manager.lib.homeManagerConfiguration { pkgs = packagesFor "x86_64-linux"; extraSpecialArgs = { inherit hunk; repoRoot = "/home/michael/dev/nix-config"; }; modules = [ ./home.nix ./hosts/ai-dev.nix ]; }`; checks include `checks.x86_64-linux."ai-dev-home"`, `"ai-dev-profile-command"`; CI `build-linux` job (ubuntu-24.04) exists solely for those
- hermes account details: shell `/bin/bash`, home mode 0750; linger enabled in hermes.yaml; Hermes creds = scoped Proxmox token, Docker read-only proxy (`http://docker-host:2375`), GitHub token
- Git state: home-infra clean at `4e54fd7`; nix-config has uncommitted changes (`flake.lock`, `home/cli.nix`, `home/ssh.nix` modified; `config/agents/skills/synced/` untracked)

## Original Request

The user approved ("Yes, let's do it.") a previously-discussed plan to implement a **home-infra PR** that converts the `ai-dev` VM from a full AI development sandbox (Home Manager via nix-config, neovim, dev tools, scratch space, management-user moshi) into a bare DMZ host that runs **only the Hermes infrastructure agent**. ### Planned edits (from the approved plan)

**Delete:** `ansible/roles/ai-dev/tasks/{home-manager,accounts,neovim,scratch,tools}.yaml`, `ansible/host_vars/ai-dev.yaml`, `ansible/roles/ai-dev/files/{ai-dev-maintenance,osc52.lua}`, `ansible/roles/ai-dev/templates/tmpfiles-scratch.conf.j2`, `ansible/tests/ai-dev-maintenance.sh` (fold the single hermes-maintenance install task from tools.yaml into hermes.yaml).

**defaults/main.yaml:** drop `ai_dev_hermes_moshi_gateway_listen`; earlyoom prefer → `(^|/)(chrome|headless_shell|node)$`; clean avoid list (remove wezterm-mux-server, fish).

**group_vars/ai_dev.yaml:** remove `user_shell: /usr/bin/fish`; keep everything else.

**role main.yaml:** remove the six imports; keep identity, bootstrap, firewall, system-maintenance, hermes, hermes-media.

**Docs:**
- `docs/ai-dev.md` major rewrite: intro → Hermes agent host only; keep remote-path diagram, terraform/1Password deploy steps, verification of tailscale/nftables/ports (moshi now default 24543); delete interactive-setup, scratch-space, neovim/OSC52, nix-config herdr config, git-identity, fish/styling checks; Hermes section "add a second host" → "add a host", drop all 24544 references. **Also fix approved drift fix:** doc says two distinct 1Password fields, but terraform reads one shared `local.scp["tailscale authkey"]` for both guests — correct the doc to one shared ephemeral field named `tailscale authkey` (user pre-approved fixing the doc, not the code).

- `CONTEXT.md`: replace "ai-dev maintenance" entry with "hermes maintenance"; adjust "Hermes infrastructure agent" Avoid clause.
- `docs/proxmox-host.md`: rewrite ai-dev row note (ballooning disabled; sized for Hermes: agent venv, Hermes-managed Node, Playwright browser).
- `docker-deployment.md`, `hermes-media.md`: no change.

**CI:** remove ai-dev-maintenance entries from shellcheck list and test runs in `_quality-gate.yaml`.

## Context for Suffix

- Workflow: work directly (no subagents); create branch (suggested `chore/ai-dev-hermes-only`), commit style is imperative sentence case (e.g., "Converge the moshi hook daemon for the paired hermes account"), push, `gh pr create`.

## Agent scratch space$
$
`/tmp` is a RAM-backed tmpfs carrying a per-user hard limit of 80% of its$
size. Agent scratch exhausts that limit while `df` still shows$
free space, and writes then fail with `EDQUOT`, which Node reports as the$
unmapped `Unknown system error -122, write`.$
$
Home Manager therefore sets `TMPDIR` to a disk-backed path under the$
management user's `/var/tmp` for shells, and Ansible sets the same value in `~/.config/environment.d/10-ai-dev-scratch.conf` for the$
lingering systemd user manager. Ansible also provisions the directory plus$
`/etc/tmpfiles.d/ai-dev-scratch.conf`, which ages the scratch root at 10d and$
reaps leftover Claude, Bun, and Pi scratch at 2d. Do not raise the quota$
instead; that keeps gigabytes of scratch in RAM.$
$
Existing Herdr panes retain the environment with which their shells started.$
After first deploying this setting, replace the shell in each idle pane with$
`exec fish`. To refresh every pane at once, stop and restart Herdr at a$
controlled time; stopping the server exits its pane processes. New shells then$
inherit the disk-backed `TMPDIR`:$
$
```sh$
exec fish$
# Or, when every pane can be stopped:$
herdr server stop$
herdr$
```$
$
`quota` and `repquota` are not installed, so read the live limit through$
`quotactl_fd`:$
$
```sh$
python3 - <<'EOF'$
import ctypes, os, struct$
libc = ctypes.CDLL("libc.so.6", use_errno=True)$
fd = os.open("/tmp", os.O_RDONLY | os.O_DIRECTORY)$
buf = ctypes.create_string_buffer(72)$
libc.syscall(443, fd, 0x80000700, os.getuid(), buf)  # quotactl_fd Q_GETQUOTA/USRQUOTA$
hard, _, used = struct.unpack("<3Q", buf.raw[:24])$
print(f"/tmp user quota: {hard * 1024 // 2**20} MiB limit, {used // 2**20} MiB used")$
EOF$
```$
$
Attribute usage with `du -shx /tmp/* | sort -h | tail` and delete stale session$
scratch directories.$
$
## Neovim exception$
$
Neovim remains deliberately outside Home Manager on ai-dev. Pacman owns$
`/usr/bin/nvim` and the temporary editor LSP/formatter packages. Ansible clones$
the public Neovim configuration into `~/.config/nvim` only when it is missing,$
with updates disabled; it never pulls, resets, or edits an existing checkout.$
An Ansible-managed site plugin outside that checkout,$
`~/.local/share/nvim/site/plugin/osc52.lua`, routes yanks through OSC 52; its$
own comments explain why paste is served from the local yank cache. Use the$
terminal's paste action to insert device clipboard content.$
$
## Tailnet policy$

Authorizing a key the agent holds avoids relying on client-side
`IdentitiesOnly`.

### First run

Ansible installs the agent, Herdr and Moshi, and deploys the scoped
credentials. Three steps stay manual because each is interactive or
secret-bearing.

Give the agent a model. Its `.env` ships as a blank template, so it has no
provider key until the wizard runs:

```sh
ssh hermes@ai-dev
hermes setup
hermes doctor
```

Pair the phone to this account. The management user's pairing does not carry
across:

```sh
moshi-hook host setup
moshi-hook pair --token <token-from-Moshi-Hooks-settings>
```

Once the pairing secret exists, the role takes over the daemon: the next play
installs the `moshi-hook.service` user unit and enables it through
`systemctl --machine=hermes@ --user`. Linger is already on, so the service
survives logout and reboot. `moshi-hook service install` cannot finish its
own enablement over sudo (no user session bus), which is why the role drives
systemd directly. The daemon keeps the default `127.0.0.1:24543` gateway
listen address: sshd permits local TCP forwarding but disables gateway and
Unix-socket forwarding, so it must stay on loopback.

In Moshi, add a host: MagicDNS name `ai-dev`, username `hermes`, connection
mode `Auto`.

Start work inside Herdr so a dropped connection does not kill the session:

```sh
herdr new infra
hermes chat
```

### Operating it

Day-to-day management needs no login to the agent account. The role owns
env-file reconciliation, opt-in package updates, and user-service restarts:

```sh
cd ansible
ansible-playbook run.yaml --vault-password-file .vaultpass \
  --limit ai-dev --tags hermes,hermes-media
# Additionally refresh the hermes account's Hermes, Herdr, and Moshi:
ansible-playbook run.yaml --vault-password-file .vaultpass \
  --limit ai-dev --tags hermes -e ai_dev_hermes_update=true
```

Updates stay opt in per run: `hermes update` follows `origin/main` of the
upstream repository. That is an unpinned, self-updating code path, which is
acceptable on a disposable DMZ guest and is a reason the agent lives here
rather than on docker-host. Without `ai_dev_hermes_update=true` the play
installs missing pieces but never advances the toolchain.

Two upstream quirks to expect in update output. The updater's own
gateway-restart phase usually fails after a successful update (it restarts
in-process against a mixed old/new checkout), so `hermes update` exits 1
despite printing `Update complete!`; the role treats exactly that
code-plus-marker combination as success because the handler below restarts
the gateway through systemd instead, then verifies the service is active.
The updater also reports stashing local changes on every run: its own npm
steps rewrite tracked lockfiles inside the checkout, which the stash dance
then restores. Both messages are expected, not symptoms.

Whenever the role changes the scoped credential env, the media-broker entries,
or a toolchain version, a handler restarts the account's enabled
`hermes*.service` and `moshi-hook.service` user units through
`systemctl --machine=hermes@ --user`. Linger keeps that user manager running
without a session; this path needs systemd 256 or newer, which Arch carries.
Fresh hosts before first-run setup and pairing have no such units yet: the
handler reports that and changes nothing, rather than starting services that
have no credentials.

For ad-hoc checks between playbook runs, the role installs
`hermes-maintenance` for the management user. It drives the same operations
through sudo, so neither a session on the agent account nor a sudo entry for
it is ever needed:

```sh
hermes-maintenance status
hermes-maintenance update
hermes-maintenance restart
```

The account itself stays password-locked with no sudo entry; the agent reads
untrusted input, so the capability to change the host must not exist on its
account at all. Direct interactive access for first-run setup and debugging
remains `ssh hermes@ai-dev` or `sudo -u hermes -i`.

### Known exposure

The observer is deliberately narrower than the Docker API. Its fixed backend
is not exposed and is the only service with a read-only Docker socket mount;
the observer projects fields instead of relaying Docker responses. It resolves
the backend once before serving requests, so a backend address change requires
an observer reconciliation/restart; a stale or unavailable backend fails closed
with a generic response. This does not make status values trustworthy: names,
image references, status text, and
health status are written by workloads and should be treated as untrusted
input. Treat the agent's credentials as revocable: delete the Proxmox token
and revoke the GitHub token if ai-dev is ever suspect.

### Optional media-broker connection

The production deployment is documented in
[`docs/hermes-media.md`](hermes-media.md). The Hermes media-broker MCP
connection is opt-in and disabled in the role defaults. The live ai-dev host
group explicitly enables it. When enabled, Ansible adds only the managed `mcp_servers.media_broker`
entry and `MEDIA_BROKER_TOKEN` reference in `~/.hermes/.env`; it preserves the

instead; that keeps gigabytes of scratch in RAM.

controlled time; stopping the server exits its pane processes. New shells then
inherit the disk-backed `TMPDIR`:

```sh

# Or, when every pane can be stopped:
herdr server stop

```

`quotactl_fd`:

```sh

import ctypes, os, struct
libc = ctypes.CDLL("libc.so.6", use_errno=True)
fd = os.open("/tmp", os.O_RDONLY | os.O_DIRECTORY)
buf = ctypes.create_string_buffer(72)
libc.syscall(443, fd, 0x80000700, os.getuid(), buf)  # quotactl_fd Q_GETQUOTA/USRQUOTA
hard, _, used = struct.unpack("<3Q", buf.raw[:24])
print(f"/tmp user quota: {hard * 1024 // 2**20} MiB limit, {used // 2**20} MiB used")
EOF

Neovim remains deliberately outside Home Manager on ai-dev. Pacman owns
`/usr/bin/nvim` and the temporary editor LSP/formatter packages. Ansible clones
the public Neovim configuration into `~/.config/nvim` only when it is missing,
with updates disabled; it never pulls, resets, or edits an existing checkout.
An Ansible-managed site plugin outside that checkout,
`~/.local/share/nvim/site/plugin/osc52.lua`, routes yanks through OSC 52; its
own comments explain why paste is served from the local yank cache. Use the
terminal's paste action to insert device clipboard content.

## Tailnet policy

The tailnet policy is managed outside this repository. Give only approved user
and iOS device selectors permission to initiate OpenSSH and Mosh traffic:

```json
{
  "grants": [
    {
      "src": ["group:ai-dev-users"],
      "dst": ["tag:ai-dev"],
      "ip": ["tcp:22", "udp:60000-61000"]
    }
  ]
}
```

Replace `group:ai-dev-users` with the tailnet's approved selectors. Grants are
additive, so a broader existing grant can defeat this containment.

The Hermes agent requires the single exception below: ai-dev as a source,
reaching one read-only port on docker-host and the Proxmox API. Keep it this
narrow. Any wider grant with `tag:ai-dev` as a source erases the separation the
guest exists to provide.

Both destinations are tagged devices (`tag:proxmox` and `tag:server`), but the
grants below scope by host rather than by tag: `tag:server` covers more than
docker-host, and this guest should reach exactly one machine on that port. Name
them in the `hosts` block, since a bare hostname in `dst` does not resolve on
its own. Read each address with `tailscale ip -4 <host>`; they are deliberately
not recorded here, because this repository is public.

```json
{
  "hosts": {
    "docker-host": "<tailscale ip -4 docker-host>",
    "proxmox": "<tailscale ip -4 proxmox>"
  },
  "grants": [
    {
      "src": ["tag:ai-dev"],
      "dst": ["docker-host"],
      "ip": ["tcp:2375"]
    },
    {
      "src": ["tag:ai-dev"],
      "dst": ["proxmox"],
      "ip": ["tcp:8006"]
    }
  ]
}
```

The Docker port is pinned a second time in docker-host's `DOCKER-USER` chain,
so a mistake in this policy alone does not expose the Docker API.

The tailnet policy is necessary but not sufficient. ai-dev's own nftables
output chain drops the whole `100.64.0.0/10` range, so the guest cannot
initiate a tailnet session even where a grant permits it. The two endpoints
above are the only exceptions, alongside MagicDNS and the telemetry collector,
and the ai-dev role asserts that the blanket drop survives beside them. Adding
a grant without the matching egress rule produces a connection that times out
with no obvious cause.

### Persistent nftables migration

The ai-dev role owns only `/etc/nftables.d/ai-dev.nft`, which is included by the
administrator-owned `/etc/nftables.conf`. On a fresh host the role creates the
small root configuration; an existing root configuration is preserved and gets
one include line (or uses an existing `/etc/nftables.d/*.nft` include). The role
validates the fragment, the staged root configuration, and the live replacement
transaction before changing either persistent file. Reload and stop operate on
only the `inet ai_dev` table; the distro service still loads the complete root
configuration at boot.

A previously deployed role file containing `flush ruleset` or `table inet filter`
is ambiguous and fails closed. Migrate it manually before rerunning the role:
make a root-only backup, copy any unrelated tables/rules into the administrator's
persistent configuration, remove the legacy global flush and old role table,
then validate `/etc/nftables.conf` with `nft -c`. Only after that conversion,
and after confirming that any active `inet filter` table is legacy ai-dev state,
set `ai_dev_allow_legacy_nft_migration=true` once to remove that active table.
The role never parses, overwrites, or automatically backs up an ambiguous root
file, so unrelated persistent rules cannot be silently discarded or resurrected.

The Proxmox `eno1` NIC uses the `e1000e` driver.

content.text:
## Hermes infrastructure agent

Hermes manages infrastructure, and it reads input nobody controls: web pages
through its bundled browser, and container logs, which are strings written by
whatever produced them. It therefore runs as its own `hermes` account, not as
the management user. `/home/michael` is mode `0750`, so the agent cannot read
the management user's GitHub tokens, SSH keys, or Claude and Codex sessions.
That separation is the point: scoping the agent's own credentials achieves
nothing while broader credentials sit beside it in the same home directory.

Ansible owns the account, installs the agent with `--skip-setup`, and deploys
its credentials. The installer clones `NousResearch/hermes-agent` into
`~/.hermes/hermes-agent`, builds a uv virtualenv, links `~/.local/bin/hermes`,
and pulls a Hermes-managed Node and a Playwright browser, so the first run is
long and the install is the largest on the VM.

ai-dev carries no Docker client. The observer speaks plain HTTP, so the
agent queries it directly, and `DOCKER_HOST` records the endpoint. Installing
the client would drag in `containerd` and `runc`, about 100 MiB of container
runtime on a guest with no reason to carry it. Nothing here prevents
installing one later; the agent simply does not need it.
The endpoint is intentionally a reduced status projection rather than a
Docker API: it supports only ping, version, container listing, and strict-name
or ID inspection, and bounded tail-only container logs (no follow). It returns
safe IDs, names, image references, state, status, exit codes, health status,
and demultiplexed container log text. It does not support stats, events,
archive operations, or full `docker inspect`; commands depending on those
routes must use an approved, separately protected diagnostic path.

### Access tiers

The agent observes broadly, acts narrowly, and proposes everything else.

| Tier | Reach | Mechanism |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Observe | Proxmox cluster and guest state | `PVEAuditor` API token |
| Observe | Sanitized container status | Read-only Docker observer |
| Propose | Any change to this repository | GitHub token, pull request only |
| Act | Nothing on a running host | Deliberately absent |

No credential the agent holds can change a running host. Remediation happens
by pull request, which `main`'s branch protection forces through review, and
which Portainer then deploys. A merge is the supervision that a watched SSH
session used to provide.

### Provisioning the credentials

Two credentials are minted by hand and kept in the Ansible vault: a Proxmox
API token holding `PVEAuditor` with privilege separation, which is read-only by
construction, and a fine-grained GitHub token scoped to this repository alone
with Contents and Pull requests read/write and nothing else. Fine-grained
tokens cannot be minted through the API, so that one is created in the GitHub
UI. `ansible/roles/ai-dev/defaults/main.yaml` names the vault keys the role
reads.

The play installs the agent without these and reports their absence, so the
host can be provisioned before the tokens exist. With them present it writes
`~hermes/.config/hermes/env` at mode `0600`, sourced from the account's
`.profile`.

### Reaching the agent

The account is a normal login. Ansible authorizes the same operator key that
reaches the management user and enables linger, so the account can hold its
own persistent Herdr and Moshi services. Either path works:

```sh
ssh hermes@ai-dev          # dedicated session, own Herdr and Moshi
sudo -u hermes -i          # from an existing management-user pane
```

Prefer the dedicated SSH session when the agent should keep long-running work
alive independently of the management user's Herdr, which is the usual case
for infrastructure monitoring. Use `sudo -u hermes -i` for a quick look from a
pane that is already open.

Each account runs its own Herdr and Moshi, both installed by the role.
Reaching the phone from the agent account means running the same pairing flow
again as `hermes`, not copying a key across; that separation is intentional.

Authorizing the operator keys grants a human entry into the agent account. It
grants the agent nothing: no key on the agent's side reaches the management
user, whose home stays mode `0750`.

Two keys are authorized, and the second one matters. SSH offers the keys held
in the 1Password agent before any key sitting on disk, and `MaxAuthTries` is
6. Authorizing only the on-disk operator key means the agent's six keys are
offered and refused first, and the connection is dropped as
`Too many authentication failures` before the right key is ever tried.

## Agent scratch space

`/tmp` is a RAM-backed tmpfs carrying a per-user hard limit of 80% of its
size. Agent scratch exhausts that limit while `df` still shows
free space, and writes then fail with `EDQUOT`, which Node reports as the
unmapped `Unknown system error -122, write`.

Home Manager therefore sets `TMPDIR` to a disk-backed path under the
management user's `/var/tmp` for shells, and Ansible sets the same value in `~/.config/environment.d/10-ai-dev-scratch.conf` for the
lingering systemd user manager. Ansible also provisions the directory plus
`/etc/tmpfiles.d/ai-dev-scratch.conf`, which ages the scratch root at 10d and
reaps leftover Claude, Bun, and Pi scratch at 2d. Do not raise the quota
instead; that keeps gigabytes of scratch in RAM.

Existing Herdr panes retain the environment with which their shells started.
After first deploying this setting, replace the shell in each idle pane with
`exec fish`. To refresh every pane at once, stop and restart Herdr at a
controlled time; stopping the server exits its pane processes. New shells then
inherit the disk-backed `TMPDIR`:

```sh
exec fish
# Or, when every pane can be stopped:
herdr server stop
herdr
```

`quota` and `repquota` are not installed, so read the live limit through
`quotactl_fd`:

```sh
python3 - <<'EOF'
import ctypes, os, struct
libc = ctypes.CDLL("libc.so.6", use_errno=True)
fd = os.open("/tmp", os.O_RDONLY | os.O_DIRECTORY)
buf = ctypes.create_string_buffer(72)
libc.syscall(443, fd, 0x80000700, os.getuid(), buf)  # quotactl_fd Q_GETQUOTA/USRQUOTA
hard, _, used = struct.unpack("<3Q", buf.raw[:24])
print(f"/tmp user quota: {hard * 1024 // 2**20} MiB limit, {used // 2**20} MiB used")
EOF
```

Attribute usage with `du -shx /tmp/* | sort -h | tail` and delete stale session
scratch directories.

## Neovim exception

Neovim remains deliberately outside Home Manager on ai-dev. Pacman owns
`/usr/bin/nvim` and the temporary editor LSP/formatter packages. Ansible clones
the public Neovim configuration into `~/.config/nvim` only when it is missing,
with updates disabled; it never pulls, resets, or edits an existing checkout.
An Ansible-managed site plugin outside that checkout,
`~/.local/share/nvim/site/plugin/osc52.lua`, routes yanks through OSC 52; its
own comments explain why paste is served from the local yank cache. Use the
terminal's paste action to insert device clipboard content.

## Tailnet policy

# ai-dev

`ai-dev` is the isolated DMZ guest. Its only NIC is on the physical
`vmbr1` DMZ, and it carries an 8 GiB disk-backed swapfile with a bounded zswap
cache. `terraform/main.tf` holds its current spec. Its sole workload is the
Hermes infrastructure agent, running under the dedicated `hermes` account
described below.

The supported remote path is:

```text
Moshi -> Tailscale private network -> OpenSSH -> Mosh when available -> Herdr
```

Tailscale SSH stays disabled, and this is load-bearing rather than incidental.
Tailscale SSH is not OpenSSH: it takes over port 22, so Mosh cannot bootstrap
through it, and it does not implement `-L`/`-R` port forwarding, which Moshi's
Browser Preview depends on. Moshi's own documentation recommends leaving it off
so port 22 returns to the OS `sshd`. Enabling it would break the path above and
fail the identity assertions in the ai-dev role.

Disabling it costs nothing in key handling. Moshi's Easy Pair appends its own
public key to the target account's `authorized_keys` during pairing, so no
private key is ever pasted into the phone. Ansible manages only its own
operator key line, leaving Moshi's entry intact.

Herdr is the only persistent multiplexer on the guest.

## Deployment

Generated cloud-init files under `terraform/files/` are ignored build
artifacts, not a credential store: rotate any Tailscale authentication key that
was rendered into one.

Before an approved Terraform run, create a short-lived, tagged, single-use
`tailscale authkey` field in the existing 1Password `proxmox_creds` item under
the `Terraform SCP` section. Both guests read this shared field: the field must
be present before `terraform plan` can render either guest's vendor data, and
this repository does not create or revoke keys.

If bootstrap fails, inspect cloud-init status and the guest's Tailscale state
without retrying blindly. A key that was consumed, exposed in logs/artifacts,
expired, or is no longer needed must be revoked in the Tailscale admin console
and replaced with a newly scoped key in the 1Password field. Record
which guest was affected, remove stale generated files, and rerun only after the
new key is available. On expiry or revocation, expect that guest to require
an explicit rejoin.

Run:

```sh
cd terraform
terraform fmt -check -recursive
terraform validate
terraform plan
```

Stop if VMID 110 or its disk would be destroyed or replaced; `main.tf` keeps a
`moved` block, so an address move is the only structural change a plan should
ever report here.
If the plan instead proposes creating all BPG-provider VMs or asks for the
legacy Telmate provider, stop: the local state predates the earlier provider
migration and must be reconciled/imported before this rename can be planned.

Then stage the guest and router changes:

```sh
cd ansible
ansible-playbook run.yaml --vault-password-file .vaultpass \
  --limit ai-dev --check --diff
ansible-playbook run.yaml --vault-password-file .vaultpass --limit ai-dev
ansible-playbook run.yaml --vault-password-file .vaultpass --limit ai-dev
cd ..
(cd ansible && ansible-playbook run.yaml --vault-password-file .vaultpass --limit routeros --tags services,oob,vlans,dmz,dhcp,firewall,bridge,vlan-filtering,default-drop,verify -e routeros_enable_vlan_filtering=true -e routeros_enable_default_drop=true)
```

The Proxmox IP configuration does not request guest IPv6, and the ai-dev role
persists the physical DMZ IPv6 disablement after networking is available. A
per-interface networkd drop-in disables DHCPv6, IPv6 link-local addresses, and
router advertisements so networkd cannot undo the sysctl policy at reboot.
The existing cloud-init IPv4 configuration and Tailscale interface are preserved.
This cloud-init template cannot guarantee first-boot isolation: its `runcmd` phase
runs after networking. Do not treat a fresh ai-dev guest as isolated until an
image/bootstrap mechanism that disables physical-interface IPv6 before network
startup has been verified. Any such mechanism must leave Tailscale IPv6
available. Legacy `inet filter` removal is disabled by default; only set
`ai_dev_allow_legacy_nft_migration=true` after an operator has confirmed that
table is role-owned. Verify generated vendor data in a temporary render before
an approved provisioning run.

## Hermes infrastructure agent

Hermes manages infrastructure, and it reads input nobody controls: web pages
through its bundled browser, and container logs, which are strings written by
whatever produced them. It therefore runs as its own `hermes` account, not as
the management user. `/home/michael` is mode `0750`, so the agent cannot read
the management user's GitHub tokens or SSH keys.
That separation is the point: scoping the agent's own credentials achieves
nothing while broader credentials sit beside it in the same home directory.
